newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR CLOSES WEAKER ON HARD UNITS.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR CLOSES WEAKER ON HARD UNITS.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar finished Wednesday's interbank session softer against the key U.S. dollar compared to its overnight levels with dealers saying it could have been quoted even softer had the central bank not injected foreign currency into the market during the day.

"The Reserve Bank started selling (U.S.) money in the market when the local dollar hit 10.7600/7800. I think they want to put a break on it's slide....maybe they think it's heading too fast towards 11.0000," one dealer commented.
Dealers have predicted the Zimbabwe dollar will reach 11.0000 by year-end, pressured down by importer demand for foreign currency which traditionally outweighs export supply during the last quarter.
After the Reserve Bank's intervention on Wednesday, the local unit settled at 10.7550/7750 against the U.S. dollar and closed at the same levels, a marginal drop from 10.7500/7700 overnight.
On the crosses, it was also weaker against sterling at 18.0415/0950 compared to late Tuesday's 17.9375/9816 and slipped to 7.0575/0740 from 7.0372/0526 versus the German mark.
Against South Africa's rand it was also quoted softer at 2.3570/3650 after ending the previous day at 2.3395/3464.
